theorems.name: check_seq_hom
theorems.note: trivial: simpl unfolds ESeq to concat(map), then map_app + concat_app closes by reflexivity

theorems.name: diverged_clean_iff_barrier_free
theorems.note: key: diverged_absorbing — (if X then D else D) = D — makes Diverged mode absorbing; proof by expr_list_rect with Plist for ESeq/EApp

theorems.name: mode_monotone
theorems.note: EIf/EWhile/EFor case-split on is_varying cond; varying → inner stays Diverged in both (incl_refl); non-varying → apply IH for inner exprs

theorems.name: not_varying_converged_clean
theorems.note: helper for cdcf_check_agreement: is_varying e = false → all inner modes stay Converged → EBarrier gives []

theorems.name: cdcf_check_agreement
theorems.note: is_varying cond = false (from cdcf=false) → not_varying_converged_clean clears cond; then IH on body

theorems.name: varying_if_flags_barriers
theorems.note: is_varying cond → inner=Diverged; then diverged_clean_iff_barrier_free: ¬barrier_free → check Diverged ≠ [] → contradiction

theorems.name: superstep_outer_diverged_error
theorems.note: F-01: Diverged entry into ESuperstep with divergent=false yields BarrierError; proof by simpl + discriminate

theorems.name: env_lookup_extend_same
theorems.note: F-02 helper: env_lookup after env_extend with same key returns the stored value; proof by unfold + Nat.eqb_refl + reflexivity

theorems.name: env_let_alias_varying
theorems.note: F-02 core: if v is varying in env then ELet x v b propagates variability; proof by simpl + rewrite Hv + exact Hb

theorems.name: env_var_diverged_clean
theorems.note: F-02: EVar under Diverged mode is barrier-free (EVar carries no barrier); proof by simpl + reflexivity

theorems.name: env_check_let_alias_catches
theorems.note: F-02 soundness: varying-aliased EVar as CF condition produces BarrierError under Converged mode; proof uses env_lookup_extend_same + app_eq_nil + discriminate

theorems.name: warp_diverged_error
theorems.note: T2-WARP atomic: check_warp Diverged EWarpPoint ≠ []; models Warp_collective_in_diverged_flow from Sarek_convergence.ml lines 153-155; proof by simpl + discriminate

theorems.name: warp_mode_monotone
theorems.note: T2-WARP quantified: forall e, incl (check_warp Converged e) (check_warp Diverged e) — warp analogue of mode_monotone; proven by expr_list_rect + diverged_absorbing

theorems.name: warp_varying_if_flags
theorems.note: T2-WARP context: forall el, check_warp Converged (EIf EVary EWarpPoint el) ≠ [] — EWarpPoint nested under varying EIf is always caught; proof by simpl + discriminate

theorems.name: return_barrier_skip_safe
theorems.note: T2-RETURN compositionality: forall m e, check m (EReturn e) = check m e — EReturn is a transparent wrapper for barrier analysis; proof by simpl + reflexivity. Corollary return_converged_clean: barrier_free e → check Converged (EReturn e) = []

theorems.name: env_agrees
theorems.note: T3-S2: uniform-variable agreement predicate between two venvs — all non-varying vars in env map to same value in both rhos

theorems.name: not_varying_uniform
theorems.note: T3-S2 main theorem: env_agrees env rho1 rho2 → is_strongly_uniform env e = true → eval vary_val fuel t1 rho1 e = eval vary_val fuel t2 rho2 e

theorems.name: not_varying_uniform_args
theorems.note: T3-S2 list variant of not_varying_uniform — mutual induction companion for EApp/ESeq

theorems.name: is_strongly_uniform_impl_is_not_varying
theorems.note: T3-S2 bridge: is_strongly_uniform env e = true → is_varying_in_env env e = false — strictly stronger predicate

theorems.name: var_free_env_irrelevant
theorems.note: T3-S2: is_var_free e = true → is_strongly_uniform env1 e = is_strongly_uniform env2 e (EVar-free means env-independent)

theorems.name: is_strongly_uniform_env_irrelevant
theorems.note: T3-S2: alias of var_free_env_irrelevant; is_var_free e = true → is_strongly_uniform env1 e = is_strongly_uniform env2 e

theorems.name: var_free_is_strongly_uniform_empty
theorems.note: T3-S2: is_var_free e = true → is_varying e = false → is_strongly_uniform [] e = true

theorems.name: closed_uniform
theorems.note: T3-S2 corollary: is_var_free e = true → is_varying e = false → eval uniform across all thread ids and variable environments

theorems.name: no_barrier_event
theorems.note: T3-S3: Boolean predicate — trace contains no EvBarrier events; used as the conclusion of barrier_free_no_barriers

theorems.name: superstep_free
theorems.note: T3-S3: Boolean predicate — expression contains no ESuperstep node at any depth; required side-condition for barrier_free_no_barriers

theorems.name: barrier_free_no_barriers
theorems.note: T3-S3 main theorem: superstep_free e = true → barrier_free e = true → eval produces no EvBarrier events; EWarpPoint may emit EvWarp (intentional)

theorems.name: diverged_clean_no_barriers
theorems.note: T3-S3 corollary: superstep_free e = true → check Diverged e = [] → eval emits no EvBarrier events; follows via diverged_clean_iff_barrier_free

theorems.name: core_frag
theorems.note: T3-S4: Boolean predicate — true iff e contains no ESuperstep and no EReturn; defines the verified fragment for check_env_sound_core

theorems.name: erase_warp
theorems.note: T3-S4: trace projection keeping only EvBarrier events, discarding EvWarp; barrier_safe uses erase_warp equality so per-thread warp events do not create false negatives

theorems.name: barrier_safe
theorems.note: T3-S4: all env-agreeing thread pairs that complete evaluation of e produce identical erase_warp (barrier-event) sequences

theorems.name: eval_check_uniform
theorems.note: T3-S4 combined lemma: simultaneous fuel induction establishing Part A (barrier-trace equality) and Part B (outcome equality for non-varying expressions); Part B feeds back into Part A for condition-uniformity in EIf/EWhile/EFor

theorems.name: check_env_sound_core
theorems.note: T3-S4 main theorem: core_frag e = true → check_env Converged env e = [] → barrier_safe vary_val env e; one-liner via proj1 (eval_check_uniform vary_val fuel)

theorems.name: hazard
theorems.note: T3-S5: witness expression ESeq [EIf EVary (EReturn ELit) ELit; EBarrier] — varying early-return guarding a barrier; models the F-04 false-negative pattern

theorems.name: hazard_spec_detects
theorems.note: T3-S5 / F-04b: after the F-04b fix, check_env Converged [] hazard ≠ [] — the spec now detects the hazard (supersedes pre-F-04b hazard_checker_blind)

theorems.name: hazard_vary
theorems.note: T3-S5: concrete thread-varying witness — vary_val 0 = 1 (nonzero, takes EReturn branch), vary_val (S _) = 0 (falls through to EBarrier)

theorems.name: hazard_eval_thread0
theorems.note: T3-S5: thread 0 evaluates hazard to (ORet 0, []) — early return, no barrier event; proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: hazard_eval_thread1
theorems.note: T3-S5: thread 1 evaluates hazard to (ONorm 0, [EvBarrier]) — falls through to barrier; proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: hazard_not_barrier_safe
theorems.note: T3-S5 main theorem: ¬ barrier_safe hazard_vary [] hazard — constructive counterexample; erase_warp traces [] vs [EvBarrier] differ across threads

theorems.name: hazard_checker_sound
theorems.note: T3-S5 / F-04b: spec/operational agreement — check_env flags the hazard AND it is genuinely not barrier_safe; closes the F-04 spec/impl divergence

theorems.name: core_frag_ss
theorems.note: T3-S6: core_frag enlarged to admit ESuperstep false body cont (negb dv && core_frag_ss b && core_frag_ss c); EReturn remains excluded

theorems.name: core_frag_impl_ss
theorems.note: T3-S6: core_frag e = true → core_frag_ss e = true — the enlarged fragment subsumes the core

theorems.name: core_frag_ss_no_ret
theorems.note: T3-S6: no core_frag_ss expression returns ORet; superstep body cannot return and cont is ORet-free by induction

theorems.name: eval_while_exits_immediately_ss
theorems.note: T3-S6: core_frag_ss analogue of eval_while_exits_immediately — a terminating core_frag_ss EWhile exits immediately (cond evaluated to 0)

theorems.name: core_frag_ss_barrier_free_superstep_free
theorems.note: T3-S6: core_frag_ss e = true → barrier_free e = true → superstep_free e = true; a barrier-free core_frag_ss expression has no superstep at all

theorems.name: check_env_diverged_no_barriers_ss
theorems.note: T3-S6: resolves the T3-S3 superstep_free side condition over core_frag_ss — Diverged-clean core_frag_ss expressions are barrier-silent

theorems.name: eval_check_uniform_ss
theorems.note: T3-S6: combined Part A (barrier-trace) + Part B (outcome) uniformity by fuel induction over core_frag_ss; new ESuperstep case emits implicit [EvBarrier] uniformly on all threads

theorems.name: check_env_sound_superstep
theorems.note: T3-S6 main theorem: core_frag_ss e = true → check_env Converged env e = [] → barrier_safe vary_val env e; enlarges T3-S4 fragment to include dv=false supersteps

theorems.name: susp_hazard
theorems.note: T3-S6: witness EIf EVary (ESuperstep false EBarrier ELit) ELit — thread 0 traces [EvBarrier; EvBarrier], thread 1 traces []

theorems.name: susp_vary
theorems.note: T3-S6: concrete vary_val for susp_hazard — susp_vary 0 = 1 (then-branch, ESuperstep), susp_vary (S _) = 0 (else-branch, ELit)

theorems.name: susp_eval_thread0
theorems.note: T3-S6: thread 0 evaluates susp_hazard to (ONorm 0, [EvBarrier; EvBarrier]); proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: susp_eval_thread1
theorems.note: T3-S6: thread 1 evaluates susp_hazard to (ONorm 0, []); proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: semantic_f01_flagged
theorems.note: T3-S6: check_env Converged [] susp_hazard ≠ [] — the env-threaded checker flags susp_hazard

theorems.name: semantic_f01_not_barrier_safe
theorems.note: T3-S6: ¬ barrier_safe susp_vary [] susp_hazard — barrier traces [EvBarrier; EvBarrier] vs [] diverge across env-agreeing threads

theorems.name: semantic_f01_corollary
theorems.note: T3-S6: conjunction — susp_hazard is flagged AND not barrier_safe; the F-01 BarrierError is a SOUND rejection grounding superstep_outer_diverged_error at runtime

theorems.name: erase_barrier
theorems.note: T3-S7: trace projection keeping only EvWarp events, discarding EvBarrier — dual of erase_warp; warp_safe uses erase_barrier equality

theorems.name: warp_free
theorems.note: T3-S7: Boolean predicate — expression contains no EWarpPoint; dual of barrier_free

theorems.name: warp_free_no_warps
theorems.note: T3-S7 trace-silence theorem: superstep_free e = true → warp_free e = true → eval emits no EvWarp events; dual of barrier_free_no_barriers

theorems.name: check_warp_env
theorems.note: T3-S7: env-threaded warp checker mirroring check_env; flags EWarpPoint (not EBarrier) under Diverged mode

theorems.name: check_warp_env_diverged_clean_warp_free
theorems.note: T3-S7 bridge lemma: check_warp_env Diverged env e = [] → warp_free e = true; ESuperstep does not flag in check_warp_env (no warp hazard at boundary)

theorems.name: check_warp_env_diverged_no_warps
theorems.note: T3-S7: core_frag e = true → check_warp_env Diverged env e = [] → eval emits no EvWarp events; dual of check_env_diverged_no_barriers

theorems.name: eval_check_warp_uniform
theorems.note: T3-S7: warp dual of eval_check_uniform — Part A (erase_barrier trace equality) + Part B (outcome equality) over core_frag with check_warp_env Converged clean; mechanical EBarrier↔EWarpPoint substitution of eval_check_uniform

theorems.name: warp_safe
theorems.note: T3-S7: same-warp erase_barrier-trace agreement predicate parametric in warp_of : tid → nat; warp_of t1 = warp_of t2 → erase_barrier traces agree

theorems.name: check_warp_sound_core
theorems.note: T3-S7 main theorem: core_frag e = true → check_warp_env Converged env e = [] → warp_safe vary_val env e; warp dual of check_env_sound_core; warp-size parameterization CLOSED (warp_of abstract Section Variable)

theorems.name: eval_concrete
theorems.note: T3-S8: eval instantiated with vary_val = fun th => th (identity); the extraction witness for the operational CMBT suite; distinct threads receive distinct EVary values

theorems.name: eval_concrete_fuel_monotone
theorems.note: T3-S8: fuel-monotonicity specialized to eval_concrete; direct application of section theorem eval_fuel_monotone; mirrored by QCheck sem:eval_fuel_monotone

theorems.name: eval_concrete_barrier_free_silent
theorems.note: T3-S8: barrier-silence for eval_concrete; superstep_free ∧ barrier_free → no EvBarrier in trace; mirrored by QCheck sem:barrier_free_silent

theorems.name: has_reachable_return
theorems.note: F-04b: Boolean predicate — true iff e contains an EReturn on some execution path; mirrors OCaml has_reachable_return (Sarek_convergence.ml lines 142–202)

theorems.name: has_varying_return
theorems.note: F-04b: Boolean predicate — true iff e contains an EReturn reachable under a thread-varying condition; mirrors OCaml has_varying_return; used by check_env_seq to detect the F-04 hazard pattern

theorems.name: check_env_seq
theorems.note: F-04b: named wrapper for the F-04b mode-threading ESeq walker in check_env; check_env_seq m env es = check_env m env (ESeq es); gives stable equations for proofs

theorems.name: check_env_seq_nil
theorems.note: F-04b: check_env_seq m env [] = []; proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: check_env_seq_cons
theorems.note: F-04b: check_env_seq m env (e :: rest) = check_env m env e ++ check_env_seq (if has_varying_return env e then Diverged else m) env rest; proof by reflexivity

theorems.name: check_env_ESeq
theorems.note: F-04b: check_env m env (ESeq es) = check_env_seq m env es; definitional equality exposed as a lemma for rewriting

theorems.name: check_env_seq_diverged
theorems.note: F-04b: check_env_seq Diverged env es = concat (map (check_env Diverged env) es); in Diverged mode the flag-threading collapses to plain flat-map, preserving existing Diverged-mode proofs
